findings.before: Only two legacy generic rules, with a generic grade ≥3 haematological warning and non-specific severe hepatic review.
findings.after: 79 source-linked rules cover actual endocrine eligibility, source organ-function distinctions, interactions, symptoms and monitoring. Unsupported cytotoxic blood-count/CTCAE treatment cutoffs are not added.

findings.before: No executable source dose or frequency for severe hepatic impairment.
findings.after: Child–Pugh C displays 2.5 mg every other day exactly as the NCCP table. It never calculates a 1.25 mg daily tablet instruction. Concurrent unresolved safety review prevents a numeric restart display.

findings.before: The same generic severe-hepatic rule obscured opposite source instructions.
findings.after: Anastrozole severe hepatic impairment is not recommended and prompts withholding pending review; exemestane has no hepatic reduction, with HPRA caution retained.

findings.before: No menopause, pregnancy, breastfeeding or hypersensitivity safeguards.
findings.after: Explicit exclusions and menopause uncertainty are encoded. AI alone does not validate an ovarian-suppression combination. Returning ovarian function prompts review before further monotherapy.

findings.before: No structured daily schedules or exact indication subdivisions.
findings.after: Continuous once-daily oral schedules and all 11 NCCP indications are represented, including 00371 neoadjuvant 4–8-month response/surgery pathway and indication-specific prior endocrine history.
Agent-specific optional bands/numeric inputs preserve anastrozole GFR <30 caution and the letrozole SmPC evidence gap below CrCl 10. No unsupported percentage reduction or false low-renal clearance.

findings.before: No practical bone-health or endocrine interaction assessment.
findings.after: Bone risk, indicated DXA/bone protection, intolerable symptoms, oestrogen/tamoxifen prescription review and relevant CYP interactions are represented without forcing generic chemotherapy side effects.
25 mg preferably after a meal, no catch-up/double dosing, consider baseline vitamin D; no automatic dose doubling with CYP3A4 inducers.

source_discrepancies.detail: NCCP broad HR-positive indications coexist with an additional eligibility bullet listing tamoxifen contraindication or intolerance. An explicit report that tamoxifen is suitable produces a review message; missing history does not block unrelated partial assessment.

NCCP p2 says severe hepatic impairment is not recommended; NCCP p1 and the linked SmPC §§4.2/4.4 describe moderate/severe hepatic caution. The card follows the stricter NCCP no-treatment recommendation pending specialist review and does not mislabel severe hepatic disease as an absolute SmPC contraindication. Child–Pugh A/B/C is the UI classification of mild/moderate/severe impairment.

NCCP p2 supplies 2.5 mg every other day in Child–Pugh C. The NCCP-linked 2019 HPRA SmPC describes insufficient data/close supervision but does not prescribe that frequency reduction. The explicit NCCP instruction is displayed with this distinction and consultant/pharmacy confirmation.

NCCP no-adjustment/dialysis-expected-no-adjustment wording is broader than the linked SmPC, which says evidence is insufficient below CrCl 10 mL/min. Low CrCl/dialysis remains a specialist review; no reduced dose is guessed.

The linked Teva anastrozole SmPC lists advanced disease, whereas NCCP also lists adjuvant indications. The linked Aromasin SmPC describes switching after 2–3 years of tamoxifen and completing 5 total years, whereas NCCP also has broader adjuvant/extended-adjuvant entries. Preserve NCCP indication codes; verify the actual dispensed product and individual endocrine-duration plan rather than silently substituting product wording.

NCCP references an August 2025 product update but links to a PDF whose visible header is 9 January 2025. The linked file was read as dated; no claim that this is the latest SmPC for every product is made.

NCCP says risk-based baseline and regular/as-clinically-indicated BMD, without a single fixed repeat interval. Any proposed 1–2-year DXA schedule must be separately cited to a guideline and individualised, not presented as an exact NCCP mandate.

Direct PDF downloads returned HTTP403; web tool text is available. Screenshot requests returned text-only ImageDisplayed markers and no image bytes. The audit checks the extracted labelled tables, does not claim visual table verification, and hashes the text snapshot rather than nonexistent PDF bytes.
